text.content:
Arcs IV–VI now have dedicated session-by-session runbooks. Use this journal as the strategic overview connecting them.

ArcLevelsDefault SessionsCore Movement
IV — The Long Return12–1513Recover Memory, Time and True Name components
V — The War Beneath the War15–1812Black Host, Returned, Wayreth, High Clerist, Palanthas, Caramon
VI — Master of Past and Present18–2010Fistandantilus, Wayreth’s confession, two-Tower siege, Abyss

Read each dedicated Arc journal before running it. Tracker guidance is embedded at session level so decisions accumulate instead of being retrofitted at the finale.

Raistlin’s story advances by conclusions that remain understandable until taken one step too far.

  1. Caramon died in a magical catastrophe and cannot be reached conventionally.
  2. Fistandantilus studied unreachable souls.
  3. The Palanthas Portal can cross boundaries ordinary resurrection cannot.
  4. The Long Return can rebuild identity and reach Caramon.
  5. Fistandantilus’s version replaces the subject’s Will with Dominion.
  6. War makes the same methods useful on a larger scale.
  7. Success convinces Raistlin that control prevents loss.
  8. Caramon’s own will proves that love and possession are not the same.

Never skip the useful stage. The Black Host must save lives. The Returned must be people. Wayreth’s ruthlessness must protect the Art. Otherwise the later argument has no weight.

pages.name: Arc V War Beneath the War Summary

text.content:
Raistlin scales private research into wartime systems, and each system creates real benefits and real dangers.

Black Host

Enemies of Takhisis bound by true names, contracts/geasa and soul seals. It works; loopholes determine whether it becomes alliance or enslavement.

Returned

Living restored defenders with names, families and personalities. The flaw is command authority: they obey ritual commands before conscious choice.

Wayreth

The Tower’s transdimensional defence can defeat armies but will sacrifice individuals if survival logic demands it.

High Clerist & Palanthas

Places visited earlier return as battlefields. Every old relationship should be cashed in for supplies, refuge, intelligence or loss.

Caramon

His resurrection succeeds. The question becomes whether he is free.

The finale is not a morality scoreboard. These are consequence families shaped by trackers and player decisions.

  • The Black Mage Remains: Raistlin releases Caramon and rejects Dominion while remaining dangerous and Black.
  • White and Black: the White Robe becomes the counterweight in a reformed Orders system.
  • The Black Peace: Raistlin’s control wins the war and creates safety under ownership.
  • The Last Sacrifice: Raistlin frees Caramon and seals himself beyond the Portal with the greater threat.
  • Master of Past and Present: Raistlin transcends restraint and becomes the final adversary.

Mix outcomes when the campaign demands it. A low War State may allow a gentler ending; a high War State can make the same moral stance materially harder without making it wrong.
